Found as RETEST-FAIL in this sweep: 'Try again' button is dead: clicking it throws an unhandled TypeError and never re-renders. Repro: injected a render-time crash on / (patched Number.prototype.toLocaleString to throw) -> root error boundary correctly rendered 'Something went wrong' with the Try again button (no Error ID line, as expected for a digest-less client error). Cleared the fault and clicked 'Try again': pageerror 'TypeError: l is not a function' and the boundary stayed up permanently (>12s). Root cause: frontend/src/app/error.tsx and global-error.tsx destructure and call the prop `unstable_retry`, but the installed Next.js 16.3.0 passes only `{error, retry}` (per node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../error.md version history, `retry` became stable in v16.3.0 replacing v16.2.0's `unstable_retry`; confirmed in dist/client/components/error-boundary.js which passes `retry:` only). So `unstable_retry` is undefined and `unstable_retry()` throws. Expected: retry callback re-renders the page; actual: TypeError, no recovery. Screenshot: qa/results/screenshots/zfinal-site-025-after-retry.png. — fix(frontend): error boundaries use Next 16.3 'retry' prop (0baedd2); re-verified RETEST-PASS (see retest-zzverify-fixes.json). Fallback UI itself (heading, notified copy, conditional Error ID, product-UI styling) matches the story; only the retry path is broken. This is a post-merge regression vs earlier passes (Next now at 16.3.0).
